# AGENTS.md — OSB (OpenSROBot, corevider/osb)

OSB is a fork of opensro-bot-lean (GPL-2.0-or-later) maintained by Corevider. Compact Tampermonkey userscript bot for `https://opensro.online/play*` (combat, loot, potions, pet pickup, town trips, restocking, walk-back). It runs in the page context and observes the game's simulation worker through a worker hook. Diagnostics are exposed on `window.SROLean`. It is NOT the game client or server.

Deeper background lives in `OBSTACLE-RECOVERY.md` and `notes/<version>.md` (release notes).

## Golden rule: edit sources, never the generated files
`osb.user.js` and `osb.meta.js` are GENERATED by `build-lean.py`. Edit the source modules (`lean-*.js`, `restock.js`, `lean-skin.css`, `build-lean.py`), then rebuild. `lean-wardrobe-core.js` is generated by `build-wardrobe.py`; edit the generator/input, not the output alone. `lean-leveling-data.js` is generated by `gen-leveling.py` from the server text data.
`vendor/bot.js` is the original reviewed assistant used as build input. Do NOT modify it. Build-time adaptations are string replacements in `build-lean.py` (they assert the original text exists; if an assertion fails, the vendor text changed).

## Layout (where things live)
- `lean-controller.js` coordinates hunting, restock, return, loot; `lean-boot.js` starts everything.
- `lean-loot.js` drops/pickup/pet collector; `lean-town.js` scroll town trips; `restock.js` merchant routes; `lean-walkback.js` return to hunt spot.
- `lean-navigation.js`, `lean-pursuit-navigation.js`, `lean-chase.js`, `lean-trap.js`, `lean-antistuck.js` movement/obstacle logic.
- `lean-leveling.js` zero-setup leveling (spots for the level, NPC gear upgrades on town trips, skills and stats).
- `lean-settings.js` defaults + per-character persistence; `lean-ui.js` panel (open shadow root `#sro-bot-lean`); `lean-stats.js` session stats.
- `lean-telemetry.js` opt-in usage statistics and the shared request lane for `api.osb.lol`; `lean-reports.js` the report window and Send; `lean-reconnect.js`, `lean-session.js` reconnect/login recovery; `lean-autostart.js` optional start on entering the game; `lean-party.js`, `lean-resurrect.js`, `lean-alchemy.js`, `lean-speed-scroll.js`, `lean-support.js`/`lean-reports.js` reports.
- Tests: `lean.test.cjs` (main integration suite, loads the generated script into a `vm` context), `lean.telemetry.test.cjs` (consent, usage statistics and reports against a fake network; run by `lean.test.cjs`), `lean.obstacle.test.cjs`, `lean.logging.test.cjs`, `lean.session.test.cjs`, `lean.browser.test.cjs` (Playwright + Edge), `lean.navigation.native.test.mjs` (needs an OpenSRO checkout).

## Commands (run from repo root)
```bash
python3 build-lean.py            # regenerate osb.user.js + osb.meta.js (runs build-wardrobe.py first)
node --check osb.user.js         # syntax check
node lean.test.cjs               # integration tests (includes lean.obstacle.test.cjs fixtures)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'   # release tool tests
git diff --check                 # whitespace/EOL problems
```
`lean.browser.test.cjs <dir-containing-playwright>` needs Playwright + Edge and is Windows-oriented; skip it unless asked. Never use the user's browser profile or live account; tests use simulated game state.
Always rebuild before running tests, because tests read the generated `osb.user.js`.

## How to work
1. Read the relevant module, its callers and its tests first. Check `git status` and preserve unrelated changes.
2. For a bug: write a regression test that fails on the current build, explain the confirmed cause, then fix it in the source module. For a feature: add tests with it.
3. Keep the bot lean. No broad rewrites; do not bring back full-assistant panels (chat, GM tools, radar, etc.).
4. Keep independent services independent: pet pickup must not pause combat; party automation must not depend on hunting. Keep manual controls and lifecycle resets working.
5. Test state-machine failure paths: missing state, pending transactions, expiry, duplicate commands, disconnect/reset, feature disabled.
6. Prefer verified game contracts over guessed command names/fields. The game source (if available at `../opensro`, under `apps/client-next/src/engine`) is READ-ONLY reference. Never modify it, and read its own `AGENTS.md` before looking.
7. Be honest about evidence: passing mocked/simulated tests is not live-server verification. Say what was and was not exercised.
8. UI labels and progress messages: plain English, short.

## Behaviour that must be preserved
- Pickup success requires a matching inventory/gold gain; despawn alone is not success.
- Pet collector has no character fallback; broad native auto-grab stays disabled; require server confirmation before selective pickup. Pets collect alongside combat.
- Loot ownership, exclusion and capacity checks apply even to name-included items.
- Obstacle recovery: unknown coverage or search exhaustion alone must never ban/stop a target; a detour owns movement until done or released (see `OBSTACLE-RECOVERY.md`). No teleporting, pose resets or collision bypass.
- Never press the game's Confirm button on the "session ended" window (it logs the user out).
- Settings are per character, stored under prefix `sroBotLean:v1:`; don't change the prefix or break saved settings without a migration.
- `window.SROLean` and its shape stay as they are: OSB Manager's bridge reads it. Share files from the previous bot (app `nixxane-bot`, prefixes `nixxane0:` and `nixxane1:`) keep importing; new exports use app `osb`.
- No data goes to third parties. The bot fetches only from `raw.githubusercontent.com/corevider/osb`, `api.github.com/repos/corevider/osb` and `api.osb.lol/v1`, plus the game's own origin. `api.osb.lol/v1` is the maintainers' own platform (decision D4, 2026-11-04) and is used only (a) for usage statistics after the player turned them on (off by default; consent is explicit, versioned and recorded) and (b) for a report the player previewed, pressed Send on and confirmed. With no consent, a declined one or a withdrawn one, the bot makes no request to `api.osb.lol`. The GitHub update check sends no user data and is on by default (operator decision, 2026-11-04); Settings, Privacy has the switch "Check GitHub for OSB updates", and with it off `lean-update.js` makes no request. Nothing is sent on the tick (`Controller.tick`) or the 100 ms Ticker; requests are asynchronous, one at a time, aborted after 15 s, and never retried faster than every 60 s. Reports are never saved to disk. On the game's own origin, `lean-unique-tracker.js` reads `GET /uniques` only while the unique hunt runs or the Setup page is shown and visible, and "Use the game site's unique tracker" is on (it is off by default, so nothing is requested until the user turns it on): at most every 2 minutes (the Uniques list's Refresh never within 30 s of the last request), with `credentials: 'omit'` and no user data. Any other outgoing host needs the maintainers' explicit approval. See `docs/telemetry.md`.

## Code style
Plain JavaScript (no bundler, no package.json), LF line endings, match the surrounding module's idiom and comment density. Python files: read/write with explicit `encoding='utf-8'`. Never edit sources with shell redirection that could change encoding or EOLs.

## Releases
Merged PRs are released automatically by `.github/workflows/release.yml` (next patch version, notes, build, tests, GitHub release with `osb.user.js` and `osb.meta.js`). PR reviews, release notes and issue fixes run on Claude (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when it is not set; see `SECURITY.md`); merging needs a maintainer's approving review (`merge-approved.yml`). See `docs/MAINTAINING.md`. Do not release a merged PR by hand as well. OSB started at 2.0.0. By hand, only when the user asks:
1. Bump BOTH version strings in `build-lean.py` (userscript `@version` and runtime `VERSION`). Versions are integer `major.minor.patch` (2.0.11 is newer than 2.0.9). Never reuse a published version for changed behaviour.
2. Add `notes/<version>.md` (short, plain language; state what was only tested in simulation).
3. Run build, `node --check`, `node lean.test.cjs`, `git diff --check`. Confirm both generated headers and runtime `VERSION` agree.
4. Commit source, tests, docs AND both generated files together with explicit `git add <paths>` (never `git add -A`).
5. Do NOT push unless the user says to. Documentation-only changes need no version bump or rebuild.

## Never
- Commit browser profiles (`browser-test-profile/`), screenshots (`lean-*.png`), `*settings.json`, `.env*`, `*.before-*.js` backups, or personal data.
- Edit `vendor/bot.js` or hand-edit the generated userscript.
- Connect to a live account or the user's real browser profile without explicit authorization.
- Spawn extra work in unrelated repos.

## Delegation (OpenCode)
- Use `@explore` for any search that spans more than 2–3 files (e.g. "who calls X", "where is setting Y used").
- Run `@review` on the diff before reporting a task done; fix real findings.
